topics.title: Lesbian Comedy & Black Jeopardy Contestant Mishap
topics.summary: A radio segment features a woman reviving an old lesbian-themed song, followed by attempts to host ‘Black Jeopardy’ with awkward and racially insensitive contestant selections. The contestants argue over names, family histories, and dating preferences while struggling with malfunctioning equipment.

topics.title: Black Man Marries Wealthy Family - Divorce
topics.summary: A black man married into a wealthy Johnson & Johnson family, receiving a prize but later divorcing. He cited evolving spiritual beliefs and perceived inequality as reasons for the split alongside claims of a small penis and racial identity disputes with his mother, creating significant tension within both families.

topics.title: Black Jeopardy & Racial Confrontations
topics.summary: During a radio segment, Howard and his guest Nicola engage in an uncomfortable discussion regarding race, Jamaican culture, and accusations of prejudice. The conversation devolves into personal attacks about relationships, family history, and stereotypes, culminating in awkward attempts at playing ‘Black Jeopardy’ with increasingly strained banter.

topics.title: Black Jeopardy Double Trouble
topics.summary: Contestants play Black Jeopardy with mixed results, including misinterpretations of James Brown lyrics and arguments about racial identity and relationships. Points fluctuate wildly between contestants, highlighting confusion over the rules and a focus on personal opinions rather than musical knowledge.

topics.title: O.J. Simpleton’s Racial Jeopardy
topics.summary: During a game of "Black Jeopardy," O.J. Simpleton repeatedly offers racially charged categories and answers based on stereotypes rather than factual knowledge, leading to chaotic exchanges about race and history. Contestants struggle with his misinterpretations while discussing Afro-Americans and their identities.

topics.title: Rob Lowe Tape Controversy
topics.summary: During a radio show segment, hosts discussed the leaked video tape featuring Rob Lowe at a Democratic National Convention and debated his actions. They referenced similar legal troubles involving Roman Polanski and Joe Walsh, concluding that even famous figures should exercise caution when recording private moments.
